title: Chicken thigh, baked, broiled, or roasted, skin eaten, from raw

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken thigh is the meat taken from the upper part of a bird's leg. When baked, broiled, or roasted, the skin is often left on, adding moisture and flavor. Thigh meat is rich in protein, iron, zinc, and B‑vitamins, especially B12.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Thighs contain more fat than chicken breast, making them juicier when cooked.
The skin helps retain moisture, resulting in a more succulent dish.
Various world cuisines (American, Mediterranean, Asian) favor thighs for grilling and roasting.
Properly crisped skin is considered a delicacy in many cultures.
Chicken thighs are a common ingredient in stews, curries, and barbecue sauces.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Thighs provide about 20‑25 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports nerve function and red blood cell formation, while niacin (B3) aids metabolism.

items.title: Minerals: iron and zinc
items.content: Iron is essential for oxygen transport, and zinc is important for immunity and wound healing.

items.title: Beneficial fats in the skin
items.content: The skin contains monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that, in moderation, support heart health.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and fat promotes lasting fullness.

items.title: Higher fat content
items.content: Thighs are more calorie‑dense than breast meat; portion control is advisable for weight management.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Chicken must be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 74 °C to eliminate salmonella.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken.

items.title: Sodium in prepared dishes
items.content: Pre‑marinated or sauced thighs can contain high levels of salt.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Thighs can be baked at 180‑200 °C for 30‑40 minutes, grilled, or pan‑seared until the skin is golden and crisp. The skin may be left on for texture or removed after cooking. Serve with vegetables, potatoes, rice, or slice into salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh chicken thighs keep in the refrigerator at +2‑4 °C for up to 2 days. Frozen thighs last up to 12 months at ‑18 °C. Thaw in the fridge, not at room temperature, before cooking.
